answer: A compass does not point true north everywhere: local iron and geology deflect it by degrees that vary street by street. The device reports its heading deviation at the moment of the challenge, and the verifier checks it against a declination survey; a garden trellis of iron, a ridge of basalt and a rooftop facing the sky each deflect the needle differently. Forging one deviation is easy, but forging a thousand matching local deviations needs a thousand real compasses in a thousand real places.
